357281.title: The combinatorial Jacobian conjecture
357281.statement:
Fix an integer $d\geq 3$. For each $n\geq 1$, let $H=(H_{i,\alpha}:i\in[n],\lvert\alpha\rvert=d)$ be a collection of complex numbers, and let $\Psi_{i,j}^{\alpha}(H)$ and $\Phi_i^{\alpha}(H)$ denote the combinatorial quantities defined in the paper. **The combinatorial Jacobian conjecture.** There exists $d\geq 3$ such that, for every $n\geq 1$, if

$$
\Psi_{i,j}^{\alpha}(H)=0
$$

for all $i,j\in[n]$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^n$ with $\lvert\alpha\rvert=(d-1)n$, then, for each $i\in[n]$, $\Phi_i^{\alpha}(H)=0$ for all but finitely many $\alpha$. This is an equivalent combinatorial formulation of the Jacobian conjecture, encoding nilpotency conditions and polynomiality of the inverse through weighted sums over labelled trees.

357395.title: Uniform recurrence conjecture for the Thue–Morse sequence in base $3/2$
357395.statement: Let $x_{3/2}$ be the binary Thue–Morse sequence in base $3/2$. A word is uniformly recurrent in $x_{3/2}$ when every occurrence of it is followed by occurrences with bounded gaps. **Uniform recurrence conjecture.** The sequence $x_{3/2}$ is uniformly recurrent: every word occurring in $x_{3/2}$ occurs infinitely often, with bounded gaps. Uniform recurrence is a basic regularity property of symbolic sequences; the source gives no proof or disproof of this assertion.

357557.title: Doolittle's local-cone conjecture for graph embeddings
357557.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a polytope and let $q\colon V(G_P)\to\mathbb{R}^e$ be a graph embedding of its edge-graph $G_P$. For each vertex $i\in V(G_P)$, define

$$
C_i:=q_i+\operatorname{cone}\{q_j-q_i\mid ij\in E(G_P)\}.
$$

Assume that every $C_i$ contains the origin in its interior, edges in $q$ are at most as long as the corresponding edges in $P$, and vertex-origin distances in $q$ are at least as large as those in $P$. **Doolittle's local-cone conjecture.** Then $\operatorname{sk}(P)\simeq q$. This is proposed as a stronger graph-embedding analogue of the polytope reconstruction conjecture, motivated by the failure of a more general statement for arbitrary graph embeddings; the source gives no resolution.

364985.title: Alikhani–Soltani conjecture on distinguishing parameters of Mycielskian graphs
364985.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n\geq 3$, and let $\mu(G)$ denote its Mycielskian graph. Write $\operatorname{Dist}(G)$ for the distinguishing number and $\operatorname{Dist^{\prime}}(G)$ for the distinguishing index. **Alikhani–Soltani conjecture.** Except for a finite number of graphs, 
$$
\operatorname{Dist}(\mu(G))\leq \operatorname{Dist}(G)
$$
 and 
$$
\operatorname{Dist^{\prime}}(\mu(G))\leq \operatorname{Dist^{\prime}}(G).
$$
 This conjecture predicts that passing to the Mycielskian does not increase either distinguishing parameter for all but finitely many connected graphs. The cited source proposes the claim; no resolution is given here.

365076.title: Zhao and Wei's Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for kipases
365076.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $GR_k(G)$ denote its $k$-color Gallai-Ramsey number. A kipas is denoted by $\widehat{K}_m$, and $R_2(\widehat{K}_m)$ is its two-color Ramsey number.

**Zhao and Wei's conjecture.** For all $k\ge2$ and $m\ge2$,

$$
GR_k(\widehat{K}_m)=
\begin{cases}
(R_2(\widehat{K}_m)-1)\cdot5^{(k-2)/2}+1, & \text{if } k \text{ is even and } m \text{ is odd};\\
R_2(\widehat{K}_m)+\frac m2(5^{k/2}-5), & \text{if } k \text{ is even and } m \text{ is even};\\
\max\{2(R_2(\widehat{K}_m)-1),5m\}\cdot5^{(k-3)/2}+1, & \text{if } k \text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source introduces this as a conjecture for general kipases and does not state a resolution in the supplied text.

365077.title: Song, Wei, Zhang, and Zhao's Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for even wheels
365077.statement:
Let $W_m$ be the wheel obtained by joining a central vertex to every vertex of the cycle $C_m$, and let $R_2(W_m)$ be its two-color Ramsey number.

**Song, Wei, Zhang, and Zhao's conjecture.** For all $k\ge2$ and even $m\ge4$,

$$
GR_k(W_m)=
\begin{cases}
(R_2(W_m)-1)\cdot5^{(k-2)/2}+1, & \text{if } k \text{ is even};\\
2(R_2(W_m)-1)\cdot5^{(k-3)/2}+1, & \text{if } k \text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

The supplied text presents this as the conjecture for general even-order wheels and does not state its resolution.

365295.title: Sum-freeness conjecture for the multiplicative inverse function
365295.statement:
Let $n$ be an odd integer with $n\ge 7$, and let $f_{\text{inv}}:\mathbb F_{2^n}\to\mathbb F_{2^n}$ be defined by

$$
f_{\text{inv}}(x)=x^{-1}\quad(x\ne 0),\qquad f_{\text{inv}}(0)=0.
$$

For $n\ge 2$, define

$$
\mathcal K_n=\\{1\le k\le n-1: f_{\text{inv}}\text{ is not }k\text{th order sum-free on }\mathbb F_{2^n}\\}.
$$

**Sum-freeness conjecture.** For odd $n\ge 7$,

$$
\mathcal K_n=\\{3,4,\dots,n-3\\}.
$$

Equivalently, for every integer $k$ with $3\le k\le n-3$, the multiplicative inverse function is not $k$th order sum-free. The claim is known for even $n$, while it remains open for odd $n$.

365360.title: Hobbs–Bourgeois–Kasiraj bipartite Tree Packing Conjecture
365360.statement:
For each $i$, let $T_i$ be an arbitrary tree of order $i$. A family **packs** into $G$ if $G$ contains pairwise edge-disjoint copies of all its members, and $K_{\lceil n/2\rceil,n-1}$ is the complete bipartite graph with parts of the indicated sizes.

**Hobbs–Bourgeois–Kasiraj conjecture.** Any family of trees $T_1,\dots,T_n$ packs into $K_{\lceil n/2\rceil,n-1}$.

This is a bipartite-host variant of Gyárfás's Tree Packing Conjecture. The source gives partial and approximate results, but the exact statement remains open.

365368.title: Prime-dimensional stabilizer 3-design conjecture
365368.statement:
Let $d$ be prime, let $D=d^n$, and let $\mathrm{Stab}(n,d)$ denote the ensemble of stabilizer states. The source considers its shadow norm $\|\mathrm{Stab}(n,d)\|_{\mathrm{sh}}$. **Prime-dimensional stabilizer 3-design conjecture.**

$$
\|\mathrm{Stab}(n,d)\|_{\mathrm{sh}}=\frac{D+1}{D+d}\left(2d-1-\frac{d}{D}\right).
$$

For $d=2$, the lower bound is known to be attained because stabilizer states form a 3-design; the conjecture proposes equality for every prime local dimension. The source gives no resolution for odd primes.

365523.title: Multiplicity–eigenvector-variety conjecture for connected uniform hypergraphs
365523.statement:
Let $H$ be a connected $k$-uniform hypergraph, let $\mathcal{A}(H)$ be its adjacency tensor, let $rho$ be its spectral radius, and let $\mathbb{V}_{rho}(\mathcal{A}(H))$ be the projective eigenvariety associated with $rho$. Write $\mathrm{am}(rho)$ for the algebraic multiplicity of $rho$. **Multiplicity–eigenvector-variety conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{am}(rho)=left|\mathbb{V}_{rho}(\mathcal{A}(H))right|.
$$

The equality is proved in the paper for hypertrees, powers of connected simple graphs, and complete $3$-uniform hypergraphs on at least four vertices; it is conjectured for all connected $k$-uniform hypergraphs.

365572.title: Cichacz's zero-sum partition conjecture for groups with one involution
365572.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite Abelian group of order $m$, and let $I(\Gamma)$ be its set of involutions. Assume $|I(\Gamma)|=1$, and put

$$
R=\Gamma\setminus\bigl(\{0\}\cup I(\Gamma)\bigr).
$$

**Cichacz's zero-sum partition conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$ and every integer partition $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ of $m-2$, with $m_i\geq 2$ for every $i\in[1,t]$, there is a subset partition $\{S_i\}_{i=1}^t$ of $R$ such that $|S_i|=m_i$ and

$$
\sum_{s\in S_i}s=0
$$

for every $i\in[1,t]$. This extends the corresponding result known for cyclic groups; the paper states that the conjecture remains open.

365579.title: The almost-regular orbit neighbourhood conjecture for generalised Saxl graphs
365579.statement: Let $G\leqslant\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite primitive permutation group with base size $b(G)\geqslant 2$. For $\alpha\in\Omega$, call a $G_\alpha$-orbit on $\Omega$ almost-regular if it contains a point of some base of size $b(G)$ containing $\alpha$; let $N(\beta)$ denote the neighbourhood of $\beta$ in the generalised Saxl graph $\Sigma(G)$. **Almost-regular orbit neighbourhood conjecture.** For any $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$, the neighbourhood $N(\beta)$ meets every almost-regular $G_\alpha$-orbit. This extends the Burness–Huang conjecture from base-two groups to arbitrary primitive groups with base size at least two; no resolution is supplied in the source.

365610.title: The constant-factor vertex-deletion conjecture for acyclic digraphs
365610.statement:
Let $D$ be an acyclic digraph, let $v\in V(D)$, and write $D-v$ for the digraph obtained by deleting $v$. Let $\operatorname{unvd}(D)$ denote unavoidability.

**Vertex-deletion conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that

$$
\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant C\operatorname{unvd}(D-v)
$$

for every acyclic digraph $D$ and every vertex $v$ of $D$.

The conjecture formalizes the expectation that adding one vertex changes unavoidability by at most a constant factor. The source gives no resolution.

365611.title: The extension conjecture for oriented trees
365611.statement:
Let $D$ be a $k$-extension of an oriented tree of order $n$, meaning that there is a set of $k$ vertices whose deletion leaves the tree. Let $\operatorname{unvd}(D)$ denote unavoidability.

**Extension conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every integer $k$, every $k$-extension of an oriented tree of order $n$ is $C^k(2n-2)$-unavoidable; that is,

$$
\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant C^k(2n-2).
$$

The source says this follows from the vertex-deletion conjecture together with Sumner's conjecture, so it is currently open with those conjectures. It concerns controlling the effect of adding finitely many vertices to an oriented tree.

365612.title: The extension-preservation conjecture for linearly unavoidable families
365612.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of digraphs. It is **linearly unavoidable** if there is a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{unvd}(D)\leqslant C|V(D)|$ for every $D\in\mathcal F$. Fix a positive integer $k$, and call a digraph a $k$-extension of $A$ if deleting some set of $k$ vertices leaves $A$.

**Extension-preservation conjecture.** If $\mathcal F$ is linearly unavoidable, then the family of $k$-extensions of digraphs in $\mathcal F$ is also linearly unavoidable.

The source presents this as a more general consequence that would follow from the constant-factor vertex-deletion conjecture. No resolution is stated.

366011.title: Maximal-status conjecture for radial Moore graphs
366011.statement: Let $G_d$ be the radial Moore graph of degree $d$, and let the **status** of a vertex be the sum of its distances to all vertices of $G_d$. **Maximal-status conjecture.** The radial Moore graph $G_d$ has maximal status for all $d \geq 3$. The paper establishes upper bounds on the status of radial Moore graphs of diameter $3$ and presents an infinite family with high status; the asserted maximality is proposed as an open problem.

366175.title: General magnetic eigenvalue disk-minimizer conjecture
366175.statement:
Let $n\geq2$, let $B$ be a constant magnetic field, and let $\lambda_n(\Omega,B)$ denote the $n$th eigenvalue of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian on a bounded open domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $|\Omega|=1$. Let $D$ be a disk with $|D|=1$. **Magnetic disk-minimizer conjecture.** If $B\geq2\pi n$, then

$$
\lambda_n(\Omega,B)\geq\lambda_n(D,B)
$$

for every such $\Omega$. Numerical results for $n=2,3,4,5,6,7$ motivate the conjecture, but the general assertion remains open.

366321.title: Equivalent Rainbow Arborescence Conjecture for at least $n-1$ colors
366321.statement:
Let $G$ be a digraph on a vertex set $V$ of size $n \ge 2$, formed as the disjoint union of $k$ spanning arborescences $A_1,\ldots,A_k$. A subgraph $B$ is **rainbow** if $|B \cap A_i| \le 1$ for every color $i$.

**Equivalent Rainbow Arborescence Conjecture.** If $k \ge n-1$, then the disjoint union $G$ of $k$ spanning arborescences has a rainbow spanning arborescence $B$.

The paper states that this formulation is equivalent to Yokoi's conjecture and may be easier to use when $k \ne n-1$. It remains open.

366341.title: The generalized congruence conjecture for $T_2$
366341.statement:
Let $T_2(n)$ denote the 2-tuple partition function used in the paper. Let $p\geq 5$ be a prime satisfying

$$
\left( \dfrac{-2}{p} \right)_{L}=-1,
$$

and let $t$ be a positive integer such that $\gcd(t,6)=1$ and $p\mid t$.

**The generalized $T_2$ congruence conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 0$ and every integer $j$ with $1\leq j\leq p-1$,

$$
T_2\left(9t^2n+\frac{9t^2j}{p}+\frac{57t^2-1}{8}\right)\equiv 0\pmod{6}.
$$

This conjecture proposes an infinite family of Ramanujan-type congruences for the function $T_2$. The paper presents it as a conjecture after discussing isolated congruences and related open problems; no resolution is supplied in the source.

366405.title: Congruence conjecture for overpartitions into nonmultiples of 4 and 9
366405.statement:
Let $\overline{R_{4,9}}(m)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $m$ into parts divisible by neither $4$ nor $9$. **Congruence conjecture.** For all $n\geq 0$, $\ell\geq 2$, and $1\leq k\leq \ell$, we have

$$
\overline{R_{4,9}}(4\ell n+4k)\equiv 0 \pmod 6.
$$

This conjecture proposes a further congruence for the overpartition function studied in the paper; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
